Wiring six working queries to call them would be the mechanical connection #272 forbids. 14 -> 12. public.awaiting_review wired as the `review` section under #276 — 0471 made it able to return a row at all. public.raise_proposals wired by the proposal-round duty under #49/#272 — 0473: nothing had ever turned an impediment into a proposal. 2026-09-18: app.proposals_sent and public.proposals_to_send left the baseline because the proposal round now calls them (0489). They were not dead code — they were #49's loop with its last link missing, so the office raised proposals correctly and never told Grant. That is what this check is for: the question is not 'is this function used' but 'is a real capability unreachable'. 2026-09-18, second pass: all eight survivors now carry a reason in `why`, which is what #272 asks for — the question is not 'is this function used' but 'is a real capability unreachable'. One of the eight, `app.suppress_delivery`, is the interesting answer: it is unreachable because the state it acts on never occurs, not because a caller was forgotten. An entry with no reason remains an admission rather than a decision. 2026-09-23, #351: check:callers was counting a mention inside a COMMENT as a call, on both sides — the database half read decide_suggestion's comment as a caller of raise_suggestions, and the repository half masked its own fix when a comment beside the new call named the function in prose. Stripping comments surfaced four functions that were always unreached and never visible: app.unarchive_document, public.model_speed, app.mail_recent, app.notebook_chat_allowed. They are recorded rather than fixed here, each with a reason. 8 -> 12, and this is the one direction this file is allowed to grow: the instrument got better, not the product worse. 2026-09-23, pass 27: app.notification_patterns' reason was FALSE and is corrected above -- the third false baselined reason this programme has found. A baselined reason is a claim about the product and must be checked like any other; a documented excuse is worse than a bare gap because it stops the next person looking. 2026-09-23: the four public.sign_in_* functions entered this baseline without being this branch's work. The ownership rule added under #351 skips a function no migration here names -- and copying the sibling branch's applied migration in, which npm run migrate requires, made them named. Each carries the branch it belongs to and whether a caller was verified there. 2026-09-23, later the same day: the four public.sign_in_* entries are REMOVED because the functions NO LONGER EXIST -- the concurrent session dropped what its own 0577 created. They were never wired; the baseline shrank because the subject went away. The check said 'now reachable' for both that case and a genuine wiring, which cost six queries to disbelieve, so it now names which of the two happened. 16 -> 12. Three more removed on 2026-09-24: the integrated candidate gives hq_document_order_set, hq_document_order_reset and hq_output the pages that press them, so the number goes down rather than the check being widened. 2026-09-30, #395 (final audit reconciliation): check:callers had been red at the baseline for two functions. app.deliverable_to was a second hand-written copy of the predicate app.delivery_refusal computes - 0627 made delivery_refusal call it (one definition, reached by the guard) and it left the unreached set; app.release_test_origins is test-infrastructure teardown and is recorded here with its reason. 12 -> 13.

why.app.create_temporary_specialist: FOR THE OFFICE, not for Grant. It is the only route by which the application role may add staff, and #128's hand-off is what uses it when a job needs a specialist the roster has not got. Only `verify:agents` names it today because no real job has yet needed one — the absence is a fact about traffic, not a missing caller, and a button for it would be Grant hiring somebody to answer a question he has not asked.
why.app.notification_patterns: THE FEEDBACK LOOP'S LAST LINK, and this entry's previous reason was FALSE. It claimed `npm run levels` and the learning page answer the question a person asks. Neither names this function or public.notification_events: checked 2026-09-23 by grepping scripts/ and by asking pg_proc for any function whose definition mentions notification_patterns -- the only row returned is the function itself. It is the ONLY reader of notification_events.outcome, which is what a thumbs up or down on Telegram and Slack writes, so the reaction buttons terminate here. public.feedback, the other half of the same press, has no reader at all. Recorded rather than wired: public.feedback holds seven rows, every one positive, none since 6 September, and building learning over a table with no signal in it is the public.contacts trap. 0580 and 0581 removed the Settings cards' claims that a press is read. What a reaction should DO is filed as #353, not guessed at here.
why.app.suppress_delivery: THE ARCHITECTURE DOES NOT HAVE THE WINDOW IT NEEDS. It stops a QUEUED message going out when an undo lands first. `public.deliveries` has only ever held `sent` and `failed` — the notifier writes the row at the moment it sends, so there is no interval in which a pending delivery exists to be suppressed. Reachable the day delivery becomes a queue; inventing a caller before then would be a control for a state that cannot occur.
why.app.teach_expertise: A SYNONYM. The Team page's expertise field (`data-f="p_skills"`) is the control Grant uses and it writes the same column through the staff writer. This is the ADDITIVE, de-duplicating version an agent or a script uses; a second control beside a working one would be furniture, which is the same judgement `action:revoke_tool` carries in the pressable baseline.
why.public.connector_sheet: REACHED ANOTHER WAY. The Connections tab renders capability sheets from the payload the page already fetches; this is the same answer shaped for an API caller.
why.public.delegation_health: AN OPERATOR MEASURE. `npm run measure` is the reader Grant has for whether delegation is real, and it is the one CLAUDE.md points at. This is the per-window detail behind it.
why.public.self_changes: AN OPERATOR MEASURE, and the Governance page already answers the question a person asks — what the office learned and why it changed (#54) — from the lessons and events readers. This is the raw ledger view.
why.public.skill_effect: AN OPERATOR MEASURE. Whether acquiring a skill changed anything is answered for a person by the learning page; this is the numbers behind it, used by `verify:acquire` and `verify:skills` to prove the claim.
why.app.unarchive_document: surfaced 2026-09-23 by #351: check:callers counted a MENTION INSIDE A COMMENT as a call, on both the database and the repository side. src/projects/sync.ts names it only in prose. Pre-existing, not introduced here — an entry with no reason is an admission, so this says what it is.
why.public.model_speed: surfaced 2026-09-23 by #351. src/providers/router.ts names it only in a comment about how routing resolves a key. Whether the basis it describes is actually read is the open question.
why.app.mail_recent: surfaced 2026-09-23 by #351. src/handlers/mail.ts names it only in prose — 'not by being pushed at him' — so whether he can pull recent mail at all is the open question, and it is the same shape as app.raise_suggestions in that issue.
why.app.notebook_chat_allowed: surfaced 2026-09-23 by #351. src/projects/sync.ts names it only in a comment about holding a fifth back for urgent work.
why.app.release_test_origins: TEST INFRASTRUCTURE, deliberately. A harness declares its run's chats and channels BEFORE it knocks (0605) and this is the same harness's teardown: it stamps the run's declarations released so the destination can be retired (0606). Only scripts/verify/lib/test-origin.ts and the isolated suites name it, because only a test run ever has a declaration to release; there is no person-facing or product caller to wire and a product caller would be a way to un-declare test traffic. #395: it was flagged NEW at the Run 5 baseline only because the check had never seen it - 0605 created it after the baseline was written. app.deliverable_to, flagged with it, is NOT here: 0627 made app.delivery_refusal (the guard claim_delivery asks) call it, so it is reached by the product.
why.app.document_adopt_version: The helper for an artifact job's revised report to become the next version of an existing document (0900). Deliberately NOT called by src/handlers/artifact.ts yet: that handler has no notion of 'revise this document', and an agent adopting a version must never approve anything (the function refuses an unapproved output). Today the same step is the person's press: document_new_version with p_by_document_id. Wire it when the handler learns which document a request revises.
